title: Construct String from Binary Tree
statement: Serialize a binary tree as a string using each node value and parentheses around child representations, omitting unnecessary empty parentheses but preserving a right child when needed.
explanation: Serialize the left child when present; if a right child exists without a left child, emit an empty left pair before the right representation.

title: Find Duplicate File in System
statement: Given directory descriptions containing file names and contents, return groups of full file paths that share identical contents.
explanation: Parse each file entry, map its content to the full path, and return only groups containing at least two paths.

title: Valid Triangle Number
approach: Sort and count with two pointers
statement: Count triples of array elements that can form the side lengths of a non-degenerate triangle.
explanation: After sorting, for each largest side use two pointers to count pairs whose sum is greater than it.

title: Merge Two Binary Trees
statement: Merge two binary trees by adding values where both nodes exist; where only one node exists, keep that node and its subtree.
explanation: Recursively add overlapping node values and merge corresponding left and right children.

title: Task Scheduler
statement: Schedule tasks represented by uppercase letters with a cooldown of n intervals between identical tasks; return the minimum total intervals including idle time.
explanation: The most frequent task determines a frame of (maxFrequency-1)*(n+1), extended by the number of tasks tied for maximum frequency; the answer cannot be shorter than the task count.

title: Add One Row to Tree
approach: Insert a row at the requested depth
statement: Insert a row of nodes with value val at the given depth, attaching old left subtrees as new left children and old right subtrees as new right children.
explanation: For depth one create a new root; otherwise find nodes at depth-1 and insert two children around their existing subtrees.

title: Maximum Product of Three Numbers
approach: Compare the three largest and two smallest
statement: Return the maximum product obtainable from any three numbers in an integer array.
explanation: The best product is either the product of the three largest values or the two most negative values times the largest value.

title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
statement: Return the average value of nodes at each depth of a binary tree, from root to deepest level.
explanation: Process one BFS level at a time, sum its node values, and divide by the level size.

title: Maximum Average Subarray I
statement: Find the maximum average among all contiguous subarrays of length k.
explanation: Compute the first window sum and update it by adding the incoming value and removing the outgoing value.

title: Set Mismatch
statement: An array should contain each integer from 1 through n once, but one value is duplicated and another is missing; return [duplicate, missing].
explanation: Track seen values to identify the duplicate, then find the value in 1..n that never appeared.
